patch_description: The metrics show the current filter tracks well (correlation 0.92, lag 0.36) but suffers from many slope changes (231) and false reversals (183), giving a very low smoothness score (0.08). The bottleneck is spurious high-frequency ripple in the endpoint estimates, not lag. Adding more linear smoothing would increase lag error, so instead I add a nonlinear "reversal suppression" post-pass: small sign changes in the output's first difference that are within the estimated noise floor are damped (partially reverted toward the previous trend), while large, genuine reversals (magnitude well above noise) are passed through untouched. This directly targets slope-change minimization and the false-reversal penalty with almost zero additional lag, since only sub-noise-scale reversals are attenuated. The noise floor is estimated robustly via MAD of the first differences already computed, so the method adapts to the signal's noise level without parameters tied to a specific test signal.
